candidates.content_text:
- Access to Mentoring, Coaching and Industry Expertise
 - Commencing February 2027 | 2 year, fixed term role
 - Starting at $88,617 + 12% superannuation
About the Opportunity 
As part of the Infrastructure Program, the Graduate Civil Engineer will contribute to projects that help shape how people move through, connect with and experience the City of Adelaide. You'll gain practical experience across the planning, design and delivery of civil infrastructure projects, working alongside experienced engineers and project teams.
From roads, footpaths and drainage to water sensitive urban design and transport infrastructure, you'll be exposed to a diverse range of projects and challenges. You'll also build experience working with consultants, contractors and a broad range of stakeholders, giving you an understanding of the project lifecycle from concept through to delivery.
This is an opportunity to turn your university knowledge into real-world experience, develop your technical and project skills and start building a career in an environment where your work can have a visible impact on the city around you.
To view a copy of the position description, please click here.
Working Rights - Eligibility
We welcome applications from candidates with valid Australian work rights, including those holding a visa with sufficient and appropriate work rights for the position. Australian citizenship is not required; however, visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
About You
To be successful in this role you will have:
 - Graduated within approximately the last two years or are expecting to graduate within approximately the next 6 months in Civil Engineering.
 - Eligible to join Engineers Australia as a Graduate Engineer (GradIEAust) upon completion of tertiary qualification.
 - Knowledge of the principles and practice of civil engineering, and emerging trends, principles and operations with an understanding of civil engineering operations and function.
 - Knowledge of Australian standards, codes of practice, authority regulations and accepted industry best practice for the design and installation of engineering services associated with Civil Engineering projects and Local Government public realm projects.
 - Skills and knowledge in conducting research to inform best practice and evidence-based approaches.
 - Ability to provide welcoming, responsive and respectful customer service to colleagues and community members, with a commitment to continuous learning, professional development and applying feedback.
 - Ability to take ownership and accountability for deliverables.
 - Skilled in communication and being able to present effectively both orally and written.
 - Strong organisational skills, the ability to successfully manage competing priorities, maintain attention to detail and meet deadlines.
Why Our Graduate Program?
Our graduate program gives you a great opportunity to start building your career, while having our genuine impact on our City and our communities. As a capital city council, we have wide-ranging responsibilities, so you'll be exposed to many different industries. This includes everything from community wellbeing to urban planning, events to infrastructure, lifestyle experiences to heritage, economic development to climate action, corporate services and many more.
Apart from gaining valuable insight into what makes our community unique, are entitled to a wide range of benefits such as:
 - Flexible work arrangements
 - A range of health & wellbeing offerings
 - On-site gym and chill-out areas
 - Social Club events where you get to connect with other colleagues
Specific to the graduate program, you will also have access to:
 - Mentorship: You'll be partnered with a City of Adelaide leader who will provide guidance and support throughout your first year.
 - Development: Approximately 40 hours of professional development over the graduate program, including participation in the City Leaders program and a collaborative group project with other graduates.
 - Regular check-ins: You'll have regular 1:1 conversation with your leader to ensure ongoing support, goal setting, wellbeing checks and guidance.
 - Hone your skills: Opportunities to develop a broad range of transferable skills relevant to various government roles federal, state and local. 
 - Networking opportunities: within the City Council and the broader government sector. 
For more information about what it's like to work for the City of Adelaide, including the benefits, please visit www.cityofadelaide.com.au/careers
About Us
Located in the geographic heart of Kaurna Country, the City of Adelaide celebrates its cultural heritage, unique natural surrounds and structures its footprint in a way that allows it to adapt to the changing needs of the community and a dynamic global landscape. Our focus is on our community's wellbeing and quality of life - investing in city improvements and on future planning, so we continue to design a liveable city where future generations can continue to live authentic and meaningful lives. This is an exciting opportunity to join our team and be a bigger part of our amazing city!
At the City of Adelaide, we thrive in an environment that is welcoming, inclusive and safe, and celebrates difference. We value and embrace our diverse perspectives and recognise the value diversity has in fuelling innovation and enabling brilliant experiences for our diverse community.
For Further Enquiries & How to Apply
All enquiries regarding this position will remain private and confidential and can be directed to Bicky Shakya on 08 8203 7351.
Please submit a Resume, a copy of your academic transcript, and a Cover Letter expressing the skills, experience and qualities you can bring to this position addressed to Bicky Shakya, Team Leader, Engineering.
Please review the position description prior to submitting an application by following the prompts to apply. 
Applications close at 11.59pm, 11 October 2026.
Please be advised this is a two-year fixed term opportunity with a starting salary at the Level 3 Classification commencing at $88,617 + 12% superannuation.
As part of the recruitment process candidates will be required to undertake a National Police Check.
We continue to work hard to ensure our recruitment process is safe for people of diverse backgrounds. 
Please note, applications received via the email address below will not be considered. We are committed to making reasonable adjustments to provide a positive, barrier-free recruitment process and supportive workplace. Our commitment to inclusivity means we welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disabilities, and candidates from with a range of lived experiences. If you require assistance with our recruitment process, you are more than welcome to connect with our People Services team on (08) 8203 7333 recruitment@cityofadelaide.com.au.

McMahon Services is one of Australia's largest privately owned construction, industrial and environmental services organisations, employing more than 1,200 people nationally. For over 35 years, we have delivered innovative solutions across civil infrastructure, demolition, remediation, industrial services and environmental projects. Our reputation is built on integrity, strong relationships, technical expertise and delivering certainty for our customers.
About the Role
Reporting to the Project Engineer, Senior Project Engineer and Project Manager, you will provide on-site engineering support across major civil utilities packages, including water, sewer and infrastructure works. Working closely with project teams, construction crews, subcontractors and key stakeholders, you'll assist with coordinating day-to-day site activities while ensuring works are delivered safely, efficiently and to the highest quality standards.
Based in Adelaide, this role offers site-based work within a fast-paced major infrastructure environment, providing outstanding opportunities for professional growth and long-term career development.

- Assist with project planning, procurement, scheduling, cost tracking and progress reporting
- Prepare RFIs and coordinate technical queries with designers, consultants and client representatives
- Monitor construction quality, environmental compliance and safety performance to ensure works meet project requirements
- Prepare and maintain project documentation including site records, reports, variations and progress claims

What You’ll Bring:
- Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or a related discipline
- Experience supporting the delivery of civil utilities, water or infrastructure projects
- Understanding of project planning, procurement, scheduling and construction coordination
- Knowledge of quality assurance, safety and environmental requirements within construction
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills with site teams, subcontractors and project stakeholders
- Experience using project management systems such as InEight, Aconex, Procore or similar
- Current White Card, Driver's Licence and ability to obtain required project clearances
What Will Set You Apart:
- Experience working on major civil utilities or infrastructure projects
- Exposure to water, sewer or utilities construction
- Strong organisational, planning and problem-solving skills
- A proactive attitude with a genuine willingness to learn and develop
- Ability to build positive working relationships across multidisciplinary project teams
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, delivery-focused construction environment
 Why Join McMahon Services?
We offer a supportive, high-performance environment where your skills are valued, and your contributions are recognised. You'll enjoy:
- Competitive salary and genuine career progression opportunities
- Long-term, stable employment with a leading national contractor
- Exposure to one of South Australia's largest infrastructure projects
- Strong safety-first culture backed by experienced operational leaders
Ready to build your engineering career on one of South Australia's largest infrastructure projects? Apply now and join the McMahon Services team.
At McMahon Services, we embrace diversity and inclusion as fundamental values. We believe that a diverse workforce fosters innovation, creativity and a deeper understanding of the communities we serve. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where all employees feel valued, respected and empowered to contribute their unique perspectives and talents.

About the role
The Civil Engineering Draftsperson will be responsible for preparing detailed civil engineering drawings, plans, layouts and technical documentation associated with Sungold Solar's solar installation and renewable energy projects. The role will primarily focus on the civil engineering components of solar projects, including site layouts, foundations, footings, equipment pads, access areas, earthworks, drainage, cable trenches, underground services and associated civil infrastructure. The successful applicant will work closely with engineers, project managers, site supervisors and construction personnel to translate engineering concepts, site information and technical specifications into accurate construction drawings and project documentation.
Key responsibilities
- Prepare detailed civil engineering drawings, plans, layouts and construction documentation for solar and renewable energy projects.
- Prepare site layout drawings showing solar panel arrays, equipment locations, access areas and associated infrastructure.
- Prepare drawings for foundations, footings, concrete slabs, equipment pads and structural supports.
- Prepare civil drawings for ground-mounted solar systems and related renewable energy infrastructure.
- Prepare trenching, conduit, pit and underground service layouts in coordination with electrical and engineering teams.
- Prepare earthworks, grading and site preparation drawings where required.
- Assist with drainage and stormwater layouts associated with solar installation projects.
- Review and interpret engineering drawings, architectural plans, survey information, technical specifications and site measurements.
- Prepare plans, sections, elevations and construction details using AutoCAD, Civil 3D or similar drafting software.
- Convert engineering sketches, concepts, calculations and specifications into accurate technical drawings.
About you
- Diploma, Advanced Diploma or Degree in Civil Engineering, Civil Engineering Design, Civil Construction Design, Engineering Drafting or a closely related discipline.
- Relevant experience in civil engineering drafting, design or construction documentation.
- Strong proficiency in AutoCAD.
- Experience with Civil 3D or similar civil engineering design software will be highly regarded.
- Ability to interpret civil, structural, architectural and engineering drawings.
- Understanding of civil construction principles, including foundations, earthworks, drainage, trenching and site development.
- Strong technical and analytical skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
About us
Sungold Solar is a growing solar and renewable energy company specialising in the design, supply and installation of solar energy systems for residential, commercial and industrial projects.
Benefits
- Full-time employment within a growing renewable energy business.
- Salary of $80,000 per annum plus superannuation.
- Opportunity to work on a variety of solar and renewable energy projects.
- Exposure to civil, structural and renewable energy infrastructure projects.
- Professional development and career progression opportunities.
- A collaborative and supportive working environment.

 DT Infrastructure, as part of the TasVic Greenlink joint venture with Samsung C&T Corporation Australia, has been awarded the contract to deliver the Balance of Works package for Marinus Link Stage 1.
 We are seeking dedicated Site Engineers and Project Engineers across Civil, Structural, and Electrical disciplines to join our team on this once-in-a-generation project.  - Demonstrated ability to manage subcontractors, project controls, and technical interfaces.
 - Excellent problem-solving, planning, commercial awareness, and communication skills.
 - Current Australian Driver's License and White Card
 Why Work for DTI

Our teams benefit from the variety of opportunities, applying their skills and experience across multiple sectors.

 - Parental leave designed for the reality of family life: Our industry leading parental leave policies are centred on flexibility to support modern family life, because at DTI, little families are a part of our one big family. 
 - Flexibility that works for you and for us: We acknowledge that everyone's needs are different in striking the right work-life integration. Whether it's hybrid working, adjusted hours, job sharing or balancing family commitments, we'll work together to make it work. 
This exciting role offers you the opportunity to work in a dynamic environment and to develop your career within a highly successful organisation. 
DT Infrastructure is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace that champions opportunity and respect. Our focus on inclusivity is active and ongoing. Women, people of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Island descent and former members of the Australian Defence Force are encouraged to apply. 
Visit www.DTInfrastructure.com.au to explore how DTI can support your career progression, unlock personal advantages and apply for our opportunities.

candidates.content_text:
HumeLink West Project
Two CIMIC Group companies, UGL and CPB Contractors have been selected by Transgrid to deliver the 130km western section of the HumeLink high voltage electricity transmission project.
HumeLink is a new 500kV transmission project which will connect Wagga Wagga, Maragle and Bannaby in regional NSW that will significantly increase the capacity of the electricity network in Australia’s eastern states. HumeLink is one of Australia’s largest energy infrastructure projects, with about 365kms of proposed new transmission lines and a range of other new and upgraded infrastructure.
The HumeLink West scope of works, worth $1.4bn, includes delivery of new 500kV double circuit transmission lines spanning 130kms from Wagga Wagga Substation to a new Substation at Gugaa, the Interface Point with HumeLink East near Gundagai and a new substation at Maragle in the Snowy Mountains for future connection to Snowy 2.0.
The Opportunity
The Civil Engineer is responsible for providing engineering and administrative coordination for the design, supply, construction and testing of the project. The primary challenges of this position are to ensure the project is completed in a safe, cost effective and timely manner to meet contractual arrangements made with the client. Responsibilities will focus on projects with earth works, in-ground services and civil structures. 
 What will a day look like in this role
•    Liaise with subcontractors to ensure job is constructed to the technical, quality and customer requirements
•    Ensure that the survey of installations throughout the project is conducted in a professional manner with all results being reviewed and accepted as correct with actions coordinated and documented.
•    Liaise with Construction Manager to ensure job is on schedule
•    Provide a focal point for all technical based queries for associated civil/structural subcontractors and suppliers.

- Commercial awareness with exposure to cost tracking, variations, forecasting or contract administration.

- Experience taking ownership of individual work packages or scopes.
- Procurement and subcontractor management experience.
- Exposure to project cost management, forecasting and commercial reporting.
- Experience working within complex or live infrastructure environments.
- Strong technical and practical problem-solving capability.
- A proactive attitude and willingness to take ownership.
- A genuine interest in progressing towards Senior Project Engineer and Project Management opportunities.
Why Join McMahon Services?
- Play a key role on one of South Australia’s most significant infrastructure projects.

This is a genuine cadet role. You'll be one of a small group of cadets rotating through the three parts of our business: projects, site and estimating. Projects

- Flexibility around uni classes and exams

- Learn alongside other cadets in a structured program
- Laptop, monthly phone allowance, uniform, boots and PPE supplied
- First aid and CPR training
- Inner city office in Windsor

Apply with your resume and a short cover letter telling us why you want to build a career in commercial construction, and which of projects, site or estimating interests you most.

You'll work closely with our centralised Bids & Estimating team, Regional Managers, Project Managers and trusted subcontractor network to make sure every bid is realistic, well-considered and set up for successful delivery.
Duties and Responsibilities
- Lead allocated tenders under the technical direction of the Appointed Estimating Manager, with particular focus on larger, higher value and more complex projects, undertaking the full scope of the Estimator role from initial document review through to submission, post tender activities and handover.
- Review tender documentation to develop a thorough understanding of the project scope, client requirements, design, procurement requirements and key commercial and delivery risks.
- Prepare accurate, competitive and commercially sound estimates, including quantity take offs, trade pricing, subcontractor and supplier quotations, preliminaries, allowances, provisional sums and contingencies, and develop the budget position jointly with the Regional Manager.
- Provide peer support to Estimators on complex tenders, assisting to resolve pricing issues, scope gaps and technical queries raised during the estimating period and contributing to the accuracy of the overall budget position.
- Identify and develop value management opportunities, alternative construction solutions and procurement strategies with Estimators, while maintaining project quality and compliance.
- Lead the development of the Department's in-house construction programming capability, including preparing and reviewing tender-issue construction programs and overseeing outsourced programming services where used.
- Work collaboratively with Regional Managers, project delivery personnel and external consultants to develop the tender strategy, construction methodology, program, site logistics and preliminaries.
- Train and mentor Junior Estimators and Estimating Support Officers, sharing estimating practices, lessons learnt and technical knowledge to build capability across the Estimating Team.
- Supervise, review and check the work of Junior Estimators, and direct the work of Estimating Support Officers, on allocated tenders, ensuring all Junior Estimator work is checked prior to the Final Tender Review and lodgement.
- Contribute to tender start up, internal review and Final Tender Review processes, clearly presenting the estimate, key assumptions, risks, opportunities and commercial position for peer review by the Appointed Estimating Manager and approval.

- Apply lessons learnt from tender outcomes and Post-Project Reviews to estimating practices, and contribute to the continuous improvement of estimating procedures and templates.
- For successful tenders, lead a structured handover to the project delivery team, clearly communicating the basis of the estimate, assumptions, qualifications, risks, opportunities and tender commitments.
- Comply with Bryant's Integrated Management System, company policies and applicable legislative requirements, and actively contribute to a safe, respectful and accountable workplace.

- 10+ years experience in a similar role.
- Diverse estimating background across a broad range of commercial construction sectors, project types and procurement models.
- Relevant tertiary qualification in Project/ Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Building, Engineering or a related discipline  (preferred).

- Proven Design & Construct experience, particularly working through incomplete or evolving documentation and identifying design, coordination and commercial risks before they become construction issues.
- Experience with ECI/D&C, negotiated and relationship-based procurement, with the ability to progressively develop a project.

- Strong value management capability, with the ability to identify practical alternatives that maintain the client's required outcome while improving cost, buildability, program or risk.
- Ability to identify design gaps and scope risk early and engage with consultants to obtain the information required to progressively firm up the construction price.
  Benefits

- Work in an environment where you can make an impact

You’ll help take projects from tender documentation through to a construction-ready handover. Your work will include measuring quantities, building estimates, obtaining and comparing trade prices, and helping procure packages as projects move into delivery.
Our estimating process is increasingly systemised. We use take-off tools such as Buildxact and are introducing AI to assist with document review and repetitive work. You’ll need to be comfortable using these tools, checking their outputs and raising questions when the drawings, scope or quotes do not align.
You’ll work with our pre-construction and construction teams, with guidance and review on key pricing and procurement decisions.
Key responsibilities
- Review plans, specifications and consultant documents, and complete accurate take-offs.
- Prepare estimates, pricing schedules and tender information using our systems and templates.
- Issue requests for quotation, follow up trades and suppliers, and compare returned prices.
- Check quotes against the intended scope and flag gaps, exclusions or unclear allowances.
- Assist with value management options and client pricing discussions where appropriate.
- Prepare trade scopes and procurement information for projects moving into construction.
- Support trade letting, purchase orders and subcontract documentation under the direction of senior team members.
- Maintain organised records of quotes, assumptions, allowances and procurement status.
- Help hand over the estimate and trade information to the project delivery team.
- Contribute ideas that make our estimating and procurement process more accurate and efficient.
About you
You’re organised, curious and comfortable working through the detail. You can measure from drawings, follow up a trade quote and spot when something needs clarification. You’re willing to use new tools, while taking responsibility for checking your own work.
You’ll ideally bring:
- Experience in residential & commercial estimating, with the ability to complete your own take-offs.
- An understanding of construction methods, trade scopes and pricing.
- Experience with estimating or take-off software; Buildxact experience is an advantage.
- Confidence using spreadsheets and learning systemised workflows, including AI-assisted tools.
- Clear communication with trades, suppliers, clients and internal team members.
- Good organisation across multiple tenders and procurement deadlines.
- Experience in procurement or contract administration would be an advantage.
Why join Evve Group?
You’ll work across distinctive residential and commercial projects and see your estimates progress into construction. You’ll be close to the decisions, supported by an experienced team, and have the opportunity to develop both your estimating and procurement skills as our processes grow.
